findings.label: Multicystic ovaries on pelvic ultrasound
findings.evidence: Ultrasound showing the left ovarian cyst A of size 3.2 x 4.3 x 3 cm and cyst B of size 10.2 x 9.3 x 9.6 cm

panels.rationale: The panel is a clinical ultrasound of a patient with Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome. The caption explicitly identifies large cystic structures (Cyst A and Cyst B) within the left ovary, consistent with cystic ovaries as a manifestation of the disease, supported by the article's context.
panels.attribution_text: Rathod et al. Solving the Dilemma: Van Wyk-Grumbach Syndrome.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.61382. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound showing the left ovarian cyst A of size 3.2 x 4.3 x 3 cm and cyst B of size 10.2 x 9.3 x 9.6 cm
in_text_mentions: Urine examination was within normal limits. Ultrasound showed normal kidney size, uterus of 6.0 × 2.8 × 3.8 cm in size, ET of 4 mm, and bilateral enlarged cystic ovaries with the largest cyst in the right ovary of size 10.1 x 6.1 x 5.6 cm (Figure 1) and 10.2 x 9.3 x 9.6 cm in the left ovary (Figure 2) with minimal free fluid in the pouch of Douglas. Her radiological examinations showed that she had eight years and two months of bone age (Greulich and Pyle's atlas).

findings.evidence: Coronal T2WI reveals large multilocular cystic lesions in both adnexal regions (white arrows)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Panel shows coronal T2WI demonstrating bilateral multilocular cystic lesions in the adnexal regions, consistent with pelvic findings associated with Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome. B: Panel shows axial T1WI demonstrating bilateral multilocular cystic lesions in the adnexal regions, consistent with pelvic findings associated with Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome. C: Panel shows axial T1FS demonstrating a left adnexal cyst with hemorrhagic foci, which is part of the case under investigation for Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome. D: Panel shows axial T1FS+C demonstrating a left adnexal cyst with hemorrhagic foci, which is part of the case under investigation for Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome. E: Panel shows coronal T2WI demonstrating bilateral multilocular cystic lesions in the adnexal regions, consistent with pelvic findings associated with Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Cao et al. Case Report: Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome presenting as vaginal bleeding: diagnostic value of pituitary and pelvic imaging.. Frontiers in pediatrics 2025. doi:10.3389/fped.2025.1736671. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Pelvic MRI showing bilateral ovarian cysts. (A,B,E) Coronal and axial T1WI and T2WI reveal large multilocular cystic lesions in both adnexal regions (white arrows) with thin internal septations and well-defined borders. (C,D) Hemorrhagic foci within the left adnexal cyst are demonstrated by peripheral high signal intensity on T1-weighted images (hollow white arrow).
in_text_mentions: (Figure 4): Large multilocular cystic masses were observed bilaterally in the adnexal regions. The left cyst measured approximately 10.7 × 6.0 × 9.7 cm and the right cyst 4.4 × 4.3 × 8.8 cm. The cysts had thin walls and fine internal septations. Hemorrhagic foci were present in the left lesion, showing peripheral high signal intensity on T1WI.

plate_findings.evidence: CT showed two pelvic lesions, one of 174 cc (right ovary) and the other of 333 cc (left ovary).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: A CT scan panel showing pelvic lesions documented in a patient with Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome, suggesting multicystic ovarian pathology. B: An ultrasound panel showing a pelvic tumor consistent with multicystic pathology, documented in a patient with Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Arellano-Llamas et al. Van Wyk-Grumbach Syndrome and Gonadectomy.. Children (Basel, Switzerland) 2024. doi:10.3390/children11070831. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (a) Tomography image of the two pelvic tumors, A: Anterior; (b) ultrasound image of a pelvic tumor, T: Transductor.
in_text_mentions: The patient was referred to our hospital, where a second ultrasound found anechoic abdominal lesions with round, dense material inside. A subsequent CT showed two pelvic lesions of 20 HU, one of 174 cc (right ovary) and the other of 333 cc (left ovary). The left one had a round interior image of 250 HU inside. The radiological diagnosis was adnexal vs. mesenteric cystic tumors (Figure 1a,b). Blood tumor markers were negative (Table 1).

Abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed well-defined, thin-walled cystic lesions with internal septations in the right adnexa/iliac fossa and left adnexa (Figure 2). Color Doppler evaluation demonstrated preserved ovarian stromal vascularity with normal arterial and venous waveforms, effectively ruling out adnexal torsion despite the marked cystic enlargement.

panels.rationale: This T1-weighted contrast-enhanced brain MRI demonstrates a sellar/suprasellar lesion with a 'figure-of-eight' appearance and superior optic chiasm displacement. This pathology is associated with pituitary thyrotrope hyperplasia, a key feature of Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome, as confirmed by the article's discussion.

in_text_mentions: I revealed a sellar and suprasellar soft tissue lesion measuring 21 mm x 11 mm x 17.8 mm, displaying a characteristic figure-of-eight appearance with superior displacement of the optic chiasm (Figure 3). The lesion exhibited homogeneous post-contrast enhancement and abutted the bilateral internal carotid arteries with preserved vascular flow. Although initially interpreted radiologically as a pituitary macroadenoma, the absence of visual field defects and the presence of severe primary hypothyroidism favored pituitary thyrotrope hyperplasia.
